review_history.resolution: Schema v2 adds the omitted setDevicePatcherNodeId execution-plan mutation and Euclidean internal family, then replaces self-declared completeness with a 44-line frozen-source lexical scan and deletion/substitution controls. It also makes mirror transitions one controller-locked ticket/epoch transaction and adds fail-closed exhaustion and primer-capacity requirements.

Schema v3 replaces the per-track segmentation-only authority with one session ExecutionSnapshot, adds machine-readable execution-consumer, sender/receiver, mapping, offline, and capacity populations, correlates ReplayComplete with a monotonic payload token, requires atomic ring batch reservation and permanent over-capacity failure, and binds track plus master dispatch to the same production gate.

Schema v4 adds derived routing, mirror, device-id, replay-order, offline, and alias-aware mutation populations. It makes routing part of the exact session revision, gives device ids a persisted non-reusing watermark and reserved-value validation, keys mirrors by device instance plus parameter uid, disables unknowable legacy compact targets, and binds the real offline call and receiver priority authority.

Schema v5 bounds stable ids to the exact 15-bit carrier domain and inventories every narrowing edge; gives the mirror state machine unambiguous Unprimed/AwaitingAck stages; completes master and producer identities; rules routing-to-master semantics; replaces drain retries with whole-block transactional staging; and adds identifier-independent mutation parsing, replay-lifecycle derivation, and an exact mutation-control count.

Schema v6 makes device ids project-global and migrates legacy track-scoped identities with an explicit reference rewrite; stages every participant in a session-wide two-phase block transaction; adds a tagged disabled legacy-automation target that survives save/load; and structurally derives receiver-independent mutations, all host event writers, narrow carriers, full replay state, undo/redo, document identity, and the complete scanner-control total.

Schema v7 carries legacy global-id rewrites through external plugin state and parameter-manifest artifact keys; fixes every Track route to one-block delivery with deterministic fan-in; gives oversized ordinary batches a terminal outcome; and replaces the remaining name-dependent carrier/document scans plus the incomplete gate declaration with type/member grammars and exact derived populations.

scope: Close AE-P1.2 G2-B item 18 with one session-level immutable ExecutionSnapshot, complete routing/execution/dispatch/carrier/document/artifact populations, project-global bounded non-reusing stable device and mirror identities, deterministic one-block Track routing, session-wide two-phase block transactions over every host event writer, a production sender/receiver primer oracle, correlated replay acknowledgement, lossless disabled legacy automation, terminal capacity failure, and track/master/offline output gates bound to the item-15 lock contract.

implementation_authorization.scope: Only the item-15 staging change and the item-18 ExecutionSnapshot, deterministic routing, project-global stable device/mirror and state-artifact identity, schema-6 automation target migration, replay protocol, session block transaction, track/master dispatch, and offline-coordinator changes declared by this packet.

non_goals: No product source is changed by this packet.
No SetBypass host-applied acknowledgement is added; successful full-frame transmission on the ordered control stream remains the defined bypass-staging boundary.
No global mirrorOnly gate may silence unrelated tracks.
Authored TrackChain and Device values remain the document/UI authority; execution modules may not consume them after migration.
Compact host indexes, pooled patcher node ids, and owner aliases are plan-local derived values and are not persisted as authored identities.
The ReplayComplete payload and mailbox acknowledgement meaning change without moving bytes, so kControlVersion advances 14 to 15 and kShmVersion advances 41 to 42 in C++, Rust, and SHM_LAYOUT.md.
Non-execution TrackStateSnapshot fields remain outside this packet; chainDevices and routing are removed rather than retained as second execution authorities.

Schema 1-5 concrete target_plugin_index values are not guessed from the current machine; only the all-target sentinel is directly migratable, while concrete legacy lanes retain their events and original compact number in an explicitly disabled tagged target.

Existing narrow device-id carriers do not widen: the exact 0x7FFF stable-id ceiling makes every 15-bit and 16-bit carrier lossless, and every narrowing boundary validates before conversion without masking or wrapping.
Transient event-ring occupancy never authorizes a drain ProcessBlock; only an already-issued exactly correlated in-flight request may complete before the identical session block is retried.

Device ids are globally unique within a project, not merely within a track; schema-6 persists one project watermark and legacy migration rewrites every track-scoped reference through an explicit {trackId, oldDeviceId} map.

A post-reservation control-frame failure is not retried as partial success: it poisons the session dispatch, accepts no output or transport advance, and quarantines every participant before future playback.
Every Track routing edge has exactly one block of delay; cycles are legal delayed feedback, and fan-in is reduced in ascending source track id, source bus, and channel order.
Legacy state blobs and parameter manifests are read through the same {trackId, oldDeviceId} migration map as the document and are written only under canonical schema-6 global-id names on save.

records.statement: Item 18 is acceptance-decidable: one session ExecutionSnapshot is the sole execution authority for deterministic one-block routing, globally unique devices, targets, patcher ownership, track and master execution; bounded stable ids and their external state artifacts cannot reuse, collide, narrow, or detach; every document restore, sender, ring writer, receiver, replay stage, mapping/output gate, carrier, master, and offline surface is mechanically inventoried; and PASS 4 is a production-bound correlated primer/ack/re-arm oracle with session-wide two-phase ordinary-block transactions and terminal capacity failure.
The original AE-P1.2 packet and its withdrawn PASS 4 are immutable inputs.
The dual-PASS item-15 lock, plan-capture, bypass-failure, poisoned-transport, and stale-waiter rulings are mandatory implementation inputs.
The census and acceptance design describe exactly frozen product 92dfdfe2 and its governed blobs.
Exactly three production hostReady true stores exist; none proves mapping plus successful bypass staging for a published runtime.

Exactly twenty-four production TrackStateSnapshot publications exist: three prepublication assignments and twenty-one atomic stores; this packet does not silently treat them as a coherent host-plan authority.

The authored execution inputs have twenty-one semantic input/mutation roots and four internal-state families cross-checked against the mechanically reproduced 67-line frozen-source mutation scan. The scan recognizes any receiver expression ending in .chain, arbitrary chain aliases, patcher/patcherNodeId sinks, and undo/redo applyDocument calls without depending on receiver names such as track, including both live device->patcher writes, master restoration, direct project parsing, and alias-laundered save-copy writes. Every live mutation and historical-document restore commits through the one session ExecutionSnapshot transaction or remains explicitly document-only.

The lower stage is MappedAndBypassStaged, not a claim that the plugin acknowledged application. It is reached only after every ordered SetBypass frame was transmitted completely; stream order places those frames before ProcessBlock. Any false result withdraws readiness and disconnects the possibly partial-frame-poisoned stream under controllerMutex.

One immutable session ExecutionSnapshot is the sole execution authority and contains one nonzero monotonic revision, the project-global nextDeviceId high-water mark, normalized one-block routing graph and reduce order, the global patcher graph and globally unique device-owner map, and every track/master plan: ordered stable device ids, resolved VST path/name and compact index, bypass, host segments, complete MIDI/audio/sidechain/aux routing, sampler identity, stable automation/mirror targets, disabled target metadata, and PatcherEvent/PatcherInstrument/PatcherAudio local-to-pooled node mappings. HostConfig plugin vectors are launch carriers compiled from that exact plan, never a second authority. Under the command-thread writer lock, an authored mutation or undo/redo document is applied to a candidate, the whole affected snapshot is compiled and globally validated, and one atomic snapshot publication commits both; failure or revision exhaustion leaves the prior document, high-water mark, and snapshot authoritative. TrackStateSnapshot.chainDevices, TrackStateSnapshot.routing, routesToMaster, and separately published graph/alias authorities are removed.

One nonzero uint64 dispatch ticket binds each host's current mapping, generation, exact ExecutionSnapshot revision and track/master plan identity, and successful bypass staging. Zero is withdrawn. Each ordinary SessionBlockPlan also receives one nonzero monotonic sessionBlockTicket shared by all of its participants. Track and master senders acquire controllerMutex in canonical participant order, reload the session snapshot and host ticket, and refuse stale plans; TrackInfo and master handoffs snapshot both tickets with their mapping. Producer transport advancement and completedBlockId backpressure admission compare the same mapping/generation/host-ticket/session-ticket/revision plus mirror stage before using a host. Neither ticket wraps: exhaustion stays withdrawn and reports terminal refusal.

Mirror readiness is one controllerMutex-guarded witness {dispatchTicket, mirrorEpoch, replayGate, causes, stage}, where stage is Unprimed, AwaitingAck, Complete, or FailedPermanent. Arm/re-arm enters Unprimed; one successful atomic mirror batch plus primer ProcessBlock enters AwaitingAck; only the exact correlated acknowledgement enters Complete. AwaitingAck never re-primes and there is no separate primed flag. Every transition updates the tuple under the owning lock; epochs and gates are monotonic nonzero uint64 values and never wrap, and exhaustion withdraws the ticket.

R13 remains valid: mirror parameters and the ReplayComplete carrying their gate token precede the primer ProcessBlock on the same ordered ring, and item 18 does not claim an intra-block parameter race. Completion waits for the production receiver's correlated acknowledgement. Gating is per host; the old global mirrorOnly scan is removed.

PASS 4 is replaced: the shared production dispatch helper permits only one per-host control-only primer while Unprimed, sends no second primer while AwaitingAck, and refuses ordinary MIDI, automation, render work, active publication, transport advancement, backpressure admission, mapping/output mixing, and master processed-output publication for that host until the exact witness is Complete. Primer output is discarded and a parked primer never joins or blocks the ordinary SessionBlockPlan, so unrelated Complete tracks continue. Atomic batch reservation publishes all mirror params plus ReplayComplete or none. Transient occupancy sends no drain ProcessBlock and follows the exact in-flight wait/retry rule; a mirror larger than C-2 for capacity C enters FailedPermanent, withdraws the ticket, and makes offline rendering fail without output.

The production offline coordinator has explicit MappingReady, ControlPreroll, ResetAcknowledged, Playing, and CountedOutput phases. It completes track and master primers while transport is stopped, rejects stale mappings in both preflight readers, then resets timeline and arms playback; no primer consumes block id, advances transport, reaches capture, or increments rendered. Each counted SessionBlockPlan preflights every contributing track and master participant, commits no ring until all can reserve, and accepts output only after every exact generation, ticket, ExecutionSnapshot revision, mirror epoch/stage, and block completion matches; preflight, event-batch, control-frame, output-write, or permanent mirror failure sets renderFailed with no partial-success claim.

Future G4 dispatch identity is {hostGeneration, dispatchTicket, sessionBlockTicket, ExecutionSnapshot revision, mirrorEpoch, mirrorStage}. TrackInfo and master handoffs carry and compare all fields against live state before producer transport/backpressure decisions, readiness, waits, mixing, metering, or output publication; aux children inherit the parent's exact identity. Any differing field compares unequal.

One clock-free fixture drives the exact shared production dispatch helper used by both track call branches and the master branch. Fake controller/mailbox barriers expose a two-host routed SessionBlockPlan, canonical lock order, preflight, ring reservations, whole ordinary and primer batches, transient and permanent capacity, exact in-flight request, partial control-frame failure, participant quarantine, active, disconnect, generation, mirror witness, candidate/committed block and transport, and output witnesses; stale track mappings and stale master handoffs are rejected. A routing fixture permutes worker/storage order over acyclic, cyclic, and diamond graphs. A separate coordinator fixture drives the real offline state-machine seam through timeline-zero and counted output.

Product implementation is unauthorized before independent semantic and evidence PASS results name this same immutable packet SHA and frozen product. Those two PASS results authorize only the declared item-15 plus item-18 scope.
The checker binds external identities, all governed blobs, exact populations, source locators, dependency closure, authorization semantics, and generated prose.

The checker counts every synthetic scanner fixture in the same exact control total as manifest mutations and self-tests population deletion/substitution, receiver-renamed chain mutations, all ring writers, type/member-based narrow producer/consumer carriers, complete replay state, renamed undo/redo and document visitors, every mapping/output/producer gate, state-artifact identity, stale-plan omission, loose mirror publication, counter wrap, premature readiness, bypass overclaim, AwaitingAck-is-complete, split-host and partial ordinary/primer publication, drain leakage, stale ack, lost regression, global gating, offline leakage, authorization drift, locator substitution, and governed-byte drift.

The bounded authority population contains fifty-seven direct chain/path hits, fifty-one routing hits, twenty-six mirror-identity hits, twenty-five legacy device-id allocator/persistence hits, twenty-five stable-device narrow-carrier producer/consumer/guard hits, forty-one compact/durable target hits, twenty-eight HostConfig/launch hits, eighty-one semantic execution/carrier/document consumers, eleven mechanically derived document restore/comparison/identity sites, seven state-blob/parameter-manifest artifact identity sites, and thirteen document-only exemptions. The implementation removes chainDevices and routing from TrackStateSnapshot, removes routesToMaster as a mixer authority, prevents execution targets from including authored chain APIs, and validates project-global stable device and artifact identities at every durable boundary.

The production surface is exactly three sendProcessBlock expressions in two semantic families, eight mechanically derived and classified daw::ringWrite callers of which six are host-block writers, one receiver reached by one dispatch edge, nine classified replay protocol sites backed by a mechanically derived thirty-six-site mirror/replay state lifecycle and the exact seven-site parameter/replay priority-and-consumption chain, twenty-three mechanically derived mapping/output/readiness/producer gates including the complete mirrorOnly lifecycle, and five capacity roots. Additions, deletions, substitutions, or unclassified missing writers or gates fail the checker.

Twelve exact sites bind the declaration, definition, and real runOfflinePump invocation at daw_engine_main.cpp:2127, mapping preflight, reset/arm ordering, counted wait/mix/increment, output writer, and producer arm observer; the checker independently derives all three entrypoint edges.

Automation, mirrors, editor/parameter requests, state capture, save/load, plugin state blobs and parameter manifests, meters, modulation, sampler and patcher ownership cross durable boundaries by one validated project-global stable device id. The global id alone is therefore an unambiguous patcher owner in SHM and editor commands even when devices live on different tracks. Compact host indexes and pooled node ids are resolved only from the current ExecutionSnapshot after controllerMutex and ticket revalidation; they are never persisted or cached as authored identity.

Complete MIDI input/output, audio input/output, sidechain, aux-child, and pre-fader routing is normalized into one directed graph in the session ExecutionSnapshot revision. Audio output has one exhaustive truth table: None reaches neither master nor a destination; Master reaches master only; Track(target) reaches that destination only and has no direct master path; ExternalInput is invalid as output and candidate compilation fails. A Track input declaration and its matching output declaration coalesce into one edge; contradictory endpoints fail compilation. Every MIDI, audio, and sidechain Track edge delivers the source's fully rendered block N-1 to destination block N, so graph cycles are legal explicit one-block-per-edge feedback and runtime/worker order cannot change same- versus next-block delivery. Fan-in reduces in ascending {sourceTrackId, sourceBus, channel} order. A sidechain Track edge is additive key input and does not change source audioOut. preFaderSend selects the pre- or post-fader N-1 signal for a Track destination without duplicating it to master. The latency plan charges one block per Track edge. A routing command mutates only a candidate document and atomically publishes the compiled graph; producer routing, TrackInfo handoff, mixer inclusion, waits, and aux inheritance consume that exact revision. TrackStateSnapshot.routing and the routesToMaster atomic are removed as execution authorities, so no old/new route combination or order-dependent fan-in can mix.

A stable device id is project-global and in [1, kStableDeviceIdMax], where kStableDeviceIdMax is exactly 0x7FFF, the narrowest lossless carrier bound; zero, kDeviceIdAuto, and kParamTargetAll are never device identities. Every narrowing producer and consumer of a 15-bit, uint16, sampler-address, patcher-flag, or UI/control carrier validates before conversion and never masks, wraps, or silently narrows. The schema-6 ProjectDocument carries one next_device_id high-water mark allocated under the command-writer lock; it never decreases on load or undo/redo, is persisted across save/load, and never reuses a deleted id, while max+1 is 0x8000 and means exhausted. Candidate compilation rejects globally duplicate, zero, greater-than-max, sentinel, id-at-or-above-watermark, or dangling device references before publication. Schema 1-5 migration first validates uniqueness within each track, reserves all valid old ids, then walks tracks and devices in document order: the first occurrence may keep its id, each cross-track collision receives the lowest free global id, and one explicit {trackId, oldDeviceId}->newDeviceId map rewrites every device, stable automation target, modulation source/target, sampler reference, and derived patcher owner before compilation. The same map retains a LegacyArtifactKey{trackId, oldDeviceId} for each migrated hosted device: load resolves both pluginStateFileName and pluginParamsFileName through that old key, while schema-6 save writes canonical files under {trackId, newGlobalDeviceId} and package assembly includes only canonical artifacts for current devices. Stale legacy aliases are ignored, never rebound. Exhaustion, missing required artifact migration, or any ambiguous/dangling track-scoped reference fails load rather than rebinding.

The mirror key is {projectGlobalStableDeviceId, parameterUid16}; value storage carries no track id or compact plugin index because the device id is globally unique. A concrete parameter command updates exactly that device instance. An all-target command expands under the current ExecutionSnapshot into one mirror entry per concrete hosted stable device, so identical plugin instances with the same parameter uid remain independent. Primer compilation resolves each key to the correct distinct track plan and compact index and refuses missing or duplicate targets before atomic batch reservation.

ReplayComplete keeps scheduling sampleTime in the block window and carries a ReplayCompletePayload containing a monotonic replayGate token. Under controllerMutex the engine allocates gate = max(lastIssuedGate, liveAck)+1, binds it to the current ticket/epoch, and fails closed at UINT64_MAX. The host publishes the maximum consumed payload gate. Therefore a retained prior acknowledgement greater than or equal to an old gate is still strictly below every newly issued gate and cannot promote a re-armed epoch.

All six frozen host-event ring writers are removed as direct writers and feed immutable staged batches; the UI-diff and host-key writers remain classified non-dispatch paths. A per-host primer remains one atomic batch, while every ordinary producer iteration first allocates a nonzero sessionBlockTicket and builds one immutable SessionBlockPlan containing every Complete track and master participant, routed dependency, exact mapping/generation/dispatch-ticket/ExecutionSnapshot/mirror identity, candidate block/time, audio-input recipe, and complete MIDI/parameter/control batch. Phase 1 acquires every participant controllerMutex in canonical stable host order, revalidates all identities, and preflights every ring for the full batch before reserving any; with all producer writers under those locks and consumers only freeing capacity, successful preflight makes phase-2 reservations infallible. A participant batch with more than usable C-1 entries enters OrdinaryFailedPermanent before reservation: one diagnostic names session, host, count, and capacity; no event or ProcessBlock is sent, no automatic retry occurs, realtime transport stops pending edit/restart, and offline sets renderFailed with no output. If any ring is only transiently full, no participant reserves or receives ProcessBlock, block/time stay uncommitted, and only an exact prior in-flight request may complete before the identical sessionBlockTicket and SessionBlockPlan retry; occupancy without one poisons transport. Phase 2 reserves and publishes every batch, then sends track ProcessBlocks and, after their matching output resolves the immutable master-input recipe, the preflighted master ProcessBlock. Any reservation invariant or partial/full control-frame failure after reservation poisons the whole SessionBlockPlan: no participant output, block id, or transport is accepted; all participants are quarantined, realtime playback stops for recovery, and offline rendering fails without output. No permanently oversized or partially successful session block is retried on live hosts.

The production ringWriteBatch used by every staged ordinary and primer participant reserves its complete event batch with one CAS, writes every reserved slot with ready=0, publishes later slots first, and publishes the first reserved ready flag last; the consumer therefore observes the whole per-host batch or none. SessionBlockPlan phase 1 proves every ordinary participant can reserve before any phase-2 CAS and classifies N>=C ordinary entries as OrdinaryFailedPermanent. A primer batch is N mirror entries plus one ReplayComplete gate. For power-of-two capacity C, usable=C-1 and the permanent mirror maximum is C-2 parameters: N=C-2 succeeds on an empty ring and N>=C-1 enters FailedPermanent without ProcessBlock. Lesser N with transient occupancy follows R-TRANSACTIONAL-EVENT-BATCH's exact in-flight wait/retry rule and sends no drain. Every preflight and batch result is consumed.

Master FX uses the same dispatch/primer helper and witness as tracks and is a downstream participant in the same ordinary SessionBlockPlan: its event-ring capacity and identity are preflighted before any track reservation, its ProcessBlock is sent after matching track outputs produce its input mix, and its failure poisons and quarantines the whole session block. Its handoff is {hostGeneration, dispatchTicket, sessionBlockTicket, ExecutionSnapshot revision, mirrorEpoch, mirrorStage, blockId, sampleStart, audio}; restart or re-arm invalidates pending and cached output, and the callback publishes processed master audio only when every identity field and session transaction match live state. Boolean hostReady/masterFxActive cannot authorize master output.

ReplayComplete gains a payload gate and BlockMailbox.replayAckSampleTime becomes replayAckGate. Bytes and offsets do not move, but meaning changes: kControlVersion is 15 and kShmVersion is 42 in C++, Rust, and SHM_LAYOUT.md, with existing size/offset assertions retained. Device-id carrier widths also remain unchanged; project-global uniqueness, the exact 0x7FFF ceiling, and checked conversions make every existing owner carrier lossless and unambiguous. Project format independently advances to schema 6.

The host receiver extracts a no-JUCE production replay-consumer seam used by handleProcessBlock. The same seam owns the production eventPriority ordering in which Param precedes ReplayComplete. Fresh-mailbox initialization explicitly resets replayAckGate, while restart/re-arm correctness remains independent of retained values because new gates are greater. An in-memory ring/mailbox test drives the real sender batch through that exact receiver, proves ordering and actual application before acknowledgement, retained high ack cannot answer a new gate, and runControlLoop still dispatches ProcessBlock to the seam.

Project schema advances 4 to 6 and writes one top-level next_device_id plus a tagged automation target: All, StableDevice{target_device_id}, or DisabledLegacyCompact{legacy_target_plugin_index, disabled_reason}. AutomationClip carries that tag and the disabled metadata beside its unchanged lane events; snapshot compilation and dispatch exclude DisabledLegacyCompact and emit a stable diagnostic naming the lane and reason. For schema 1-5, kParamTargetAll becomes All, an existing target_device_id becomes StableDevice after global-id migration, and every concrete legacy target_plugin_index is unknowable without the historical resolution set and becomes DisabledLegacyCompact with diagnostic reason legacy_compact_unresolvable and the exact original number; it is never mapped through the current machine's compaction. Schema 6 rejects untagged target_plugin_index, validates global StableDevice ids and the project watermark before publication, and round-trips every target tag, disabled reason, legacy number, and lane event exactly.

test_cases.statement: A zero dispatch ticket refuses every ProcessBlock and every audio mapping read.
Each of the three old hostReady true paths reaches the one staged publication helper; deleting any path from the fixture population fails.

An offline or realtime dispatcher that loaded ExecutionSnapshot N and parks on controllerMutex refuses after snapshot N+1 commits; authored mutation or undo/redo without publication leaves every execution consumer on N, and one publication switches the project-global device map/watermark, host map, bypass, segments, complete routing/mixer inclusion, patcher graph/ownership, automation tags, meters, sampler, modulation, and master together.

Every included multi-slot execution plan produces exactly one ordered SetBypass attempt per resolvable VST slot before the ticket publishes; non-VST topology affects segmentation but produces no SetBypass, and hostless aux produces neither host dispatch nor bypass.
A forced partial-frame SetBypass failure leaves the ticket zero, requests recovery, disconnects under controllerMutex, and a stale waiter sends no ProcessBlock after acquiring.

With a non-empty mirror and ack parked below the payload gate, the actual shared production sender atomically moves Unprimed to AwaitingAck by emitting one control-only parameter-plus-gate batch and its primer ProcessBlock while ordinary work, active, track output, and master processed output remain absent; primer output is discarded.
A second producer step in AwaitingAck with ack still below gate remains AwaitingAck, emits neither a second primer nor an ordinary sentinel, and has no hidden primed flag.

For capacity C, ringWriteBatch accepts exactly C-2 mirror parameters plus ReplayComplete on an empty ring; with transient occupancy it reserves none, sends no ProcessBlock, waits only for the exact already-issued in-flight request, and retries the identical batch and block after matching completion. Every result is consumed and no prefix is visible before the first reserved ready flag publishes last.

A retained prior ack at or above the old gate remains below the newly allocated payload gate; gate-minus-one stays AwaitingAck, the exact gate transitions the same ticket/epoch to Complete under controllerMutex, and only the next dispatch may carry the ordinary sentinel.
Overflow re-arm advances the epoch, returns readiness to Unprimed, refuses the sentinel again, and cannot be completed by the prior epoch's ack.
A parked AwaitingAck primer on track A never suppresses ordinary dispatch and output for Complete track B.

The real offline coordinator completes track and master control pre-roll while stopped, rejects stale preflight mappings, acknowledges reset, then produces tick-zero as counted block one; primers change no transport, block count, captured output, WAV frames, or master handoff.

TrackInfo, aux-child copies, and master handoffs compare {hostGeneration, dispatchTicket, sessionBlockTicket, ExecutionSnapshot revision, mirrorEpoch, mirrorStage}; any differing field refuses readiness, waits, meters, mixing, or output.

Execution modules cannot name TrackStateSnapshot.chainDevices/routing, routesToMaster, authored Device/TrackChain, runtime.config plugin vectors, compact persisted targets, pooled authored node ids, or masterFxActive as authority; direct and alias-laundered negative fixtures fail the scanner.

Track reorder, unresolved VST insertion, and patcher reassembly preserve automation, mirror, editor, state, meter, modulation, sampler and patcher targets by project-global stable device id while plan-local compact indexes change.

A routing mutation parked between candidate compilation and publication changes no producer or mixer behavior; one session publication switches the normalized MIDI/audio/sidechain/aux graph, one-block latency plan, deterministic fan-in order, and master inclusion together, and every stale TrackInfo revision is refused. The exhaustive audioOut table proves None has no sink, Master is master-only, Track(target) is destination-only, ExternalInput is rejected, sidechain Track is additive without changing audioOut, and preFaderSend selects the delayed Track-send signal without a master duplicate.

Project-wide add-delete-add never reuses a device id, schema 6 round-trips one top-level next_device_id, undo/redo cannot lower its live high-water mark, and global duplicate, per-track duplicate, zero, auto-sentinel, greater-than-0x7FFF, id-at-or-above-watermark, dangling-reference, ambiguous migration, and exhausted candidates all fail before publication without changing the prior snapshot. Device id 0x7FFF round-trips losslessly through every 15-bit, uint16, sampler-address, patcher-flag, UI, and control carrier; 0x8000 is rejected at every boundary and means an exhausted watermark.

Two same-plugin instances on different tracks with the same parameter uid retain independent {projectGlobalDeviceId, uid16} mirror entries; a concrete update primes only its instance, an all-target update expands to both, and each batch entry resolves to the correct track plan and distinct compact index.

A mirror with C-1 parameters enters FailedPermanent immediately, withdraws the ticket, emits one diagnostic, sends no primer or ordinary ProcessBlock, and makes offline render terminate with renderFailed and no output; C-2 is the exact success boundary.

The production ringWriteBatch sender feeds the no-JUCE helper called by handleProcessBlock; params are applied before ReplayComplete, ack publishes only the consumed payload gate, and deleting either production call edge fails.

Restart, session abort, or mirror re-arm between master processing and publication changes generation/dispatchTicket/sessionBlockTicket or mirrorEpoch/mirrorStage and rejects the old handoff; matching current identity publishes exactly one processed block, and Unprimed/AwaitingAck/FailedPermanent stages pass no processed master output.

The production offline state machine refuses Playing before all contributing track and master witnesses are Complete and reset is acknowledged; every counted callback has one wholly committed SessionBlockPlan and matching master completion, any participant failure produces no partial WAV, and the successful frame count is exactly countedBlocks*blockSize.
awaitAnyReadyTrack and awaitAllReadyTracks reject a stale TrackInfo mapping exactly as process and awaitNextBlock do; a current mapping with the same readiness values succeeds.

C++ engine/host handshake uses kControlVersion 15; C++ and Rust SHM versions are 42; project schema is 6; ReplayCompletePayload, BlockMailbox, and device-id carrier sizes/offsets remain asserted, globally unique id 0x7FFF is lossless, and old protocol semantic versions are rejected.

After a successful wrapped or contiguous reservation, a consumer racing every producer publication observes no batch entry until all later slots are ready and the first reserved ready flag publishes last; it then consumes the complete ordered ordinary-event or parameter-plus-gate batch.

Every participant's ordinary MIDI/parameter/control batch commits only inside the session two-phase protocol: C or more entries against usable C-1 enter OrdinaryFailedPermanent without any prefix or ProcessBlock and terminate realtime/offline as specified, while transient occupancy on any participant publishes no prefix anywhere and a successful retry uses the identical sessionBlockTicket, identities, block id, and bytes.

Transient occupancy never emits a drain ProcessBlock. Only an exact preceding in-flight request for the occupied participant may complete before the identical whole-session retry; a mismatched request or occupancy without one poisons transport and disconnects every participant, so deferred or discarded audio leaves no hidden MIDI or parameter state.

The producer transport gate and completedBlockId backpressure gate both compare mapping, host generation, dispatch ticket, sessionBlockTicket, ExecutionSnapshot revision, mirror epoch, and mirror stage; changing any field prevents transport advancement, backpressure admission, and ProcessBlock dispatch.

Two tracks both carrying legacy device 1 migrate through an explicit {trackId, oldDeviceId} map to distinct global ids; every automation, mirror, modulation, sampler, patcher-owner, UI, document-comparison, plugin-state blob, and parameter-manifest identity follows its device, schema 6 round-trips one project next_device_id, and undo/redo preserves the watermark without reuse.

A two-host routed block with capacity on A and transient occupancy on B commits neither host during preflight and retries the identical sessionBlockTicket and SessionBlockPlan after B's exact prior request completes. If B's ProcessBlock frame fails after reservation, A output is rejected, transport and block id do not advance, every participant is quarantined, realtime stops for recovery, and offline fails without output.

A schema 1-5 concrete target_plugin_index loads as DisabledLegacyCompact with its original index and complete lane events; old-load to schema-6-save to schema-6-load preserves the disabled tag, reason, index, and events exactly, never dispatches it, and never emits an active target_plugin_index.

All eight frozen daw::ringWrite call sites are classified: the four ordinary and two mirror host writers migrate to SessionBlockPlan staging, while the UI-diff and host-key non-dispatch writers remain explicitly outside the host block transaction.
